title: Where the dust settles
briefing: The plain is flat and firm — there's no better ground to build on. But the dust plumes hang over the horizon, and we don't know how much they block the sun. Measure it before we trust the panels.
goal: Measure the dust layer on the glass crust and place a relay on the rock knoll.

main_sample.label: The Glass Crust
main_sample.text: The dust settles in a thin, greasy layer. A clean panel loses a quarter of its output in a few days. We'll need cleaning and storage.

risk_sample.label: The Old Riverbed
risk_sample.text: Under the dust lie round stones, worn smooth by water long ago. There's still moisture two meters down.

routes.label: Around the plume
routes.description: A wide arc south around the dust. Longer, but with clear sight.

routes.label: Through the dust plume
routes.description: Straight through. Visibility drops, and the dust wears on the suit.

evacuation: The visor is gray with dust, and energy is low. ARK: “I can see you, even when you can't see anything. Follow the arrow. I'll lead you home.”

findings.main: Sere: The dust costs us a quarter of the sunlight. Batteries and cleaning are not optional.
findings.risk: Sere: There is water under the old riverbed.
findings.relay: Sere: The relay stands in the open. It sees everything, but needs regular cleaning.
